$comment: The vocabulary of the APR format: every registered expectedDataType and every enumerated attribute value, in one machine-readable place. Previously these facts lived in five: the JSON Schema's examples, specification 4.7, 4.9 and 8.2.1, and CelBinding.cs. Anything stated in more than one place can disagree with itself, which this project has had to fix twice already - once as a security hole.

expectedDataType.$comment: An OPEN registry (specification 4.7). An unrecognised value MUST degrade to a text field rather than error - that is what lets this list grow without breaking existing readers. Every hint here is advisory: it never constrains what may be stored, only how a renderer presents the field, what it writes when it controls the value, and what the expression profile can compute with.

types.description: A single line of free text.
types.notes: The fallback for any unrecognised type.
Hidden characters are reported as advisories, never stripped (specification 7.3.1).
As with email, suspicious characters are surfaced rather than removed.

A value that will not parse does not bind, so expressions degrade rather than defaulting. min and max are the earliest and latest suggested values, written in the canonical form for this type. A response outside them is still valid.
min and max are the earliest and latest suggested values, written in the canonical form for this type. A response outside them is still valid.
min and max are the earliest and latest suggested values, written in the canonical form for this type. A response outside them is still valid.

types.canonicalWriteForm: digits with . as the decimal separator, no grouping
alsoAcceptedOnRead: any string, including words and symbols
types.notes: An empty or unparseable value is an error to the expression profile, never zero.

types.canonicalWriteForm: digits with . as the decimal separator, no grouping

types.notes: true/false rather than yes/no because yes is English, and this format renders to speech, to other languages, and into database columns. suggestedValues names the two options ("Yes"/"No", "Agree"/"Disagree") so a renderer can label them the way the author asked. It does not constrain the response, and the CEL type stays bool.

types.description: One choice from an offered list.
types.canonicalWriteForm: exactly one value, verbatim from suggestedValues
alsoAcceptedOnRead: any string, including values not offered
types.notes: suggestedValues offers options; a response outside the list is still valid.

types.description: Several choices from an offered list.
types.canonicalWriteForm: selections separated by \n (U+000A), one per line
types.notes: Newline rather than comma because a suggested value may itself contain a comma - 'Bloomfield, CT' is an ordinary option on a municipal form, and comma separation would split one selection into two.
What the response contains is not yet specified - see specification 13.

types.description: A reference to an attached file.
types.notes: Attachments have no defined representation yet - see specification 13.

types.description: Text the renderer should mask while it is being typed.
types.notes: A presentation request only. The response is stored as plain text like every other response - the format has no encryption, and masking on screen is not confidentiality at rest.

types.description: A number chosen from a bounded range, typically a slider.
types.notes: min, max and step describe the slider a renderer should offer. They are advisory like every other hint: a response outside the bounds is valid, and a reader that ignores them offers a plain number field instead.
Any text remains a valid response; "the blue one from the brochure" is a legitimate answer that no colour picker can express.

enumeratedValues.$comment: Closed vocabularies. Unlike expectedDataType, an unrecognised value here is an error.

document.version.pattern: MAJOR.MINOR with an optional pre-release suffix
document.version.notes: A newer MINOR is readable; a different MAJOR is rejected (specification 1.3.1).

section.kind.notes: table is a claim about structure, not appearance (specification 4.5).

section.canAddRows.notes: Whether a filler may add or remove instances. Fixed is the safe default.

responseMetadata.source.notes: Distinguishes a stale computed value from a correction someone typed (specification 8.6).

signature.canonicalization.notes: A verifier that does not recognise the value MUST report the signature unverifiable, never invalid.

universalHints.$comment: Meaningful on any prompt, whatever its type.
